memo.decision: (1) PLAN and CCG inspection lines process the LNG carrier and other inbound vessels through a formal but expedited 'customs clearance' procedure at the designated anchorage—non-destructive boarding, cargo manifest verification, and release after a 24-48 hour delay—rather than turning it back outright, preserving the legal fiction that this is sovereign customs enforcement rather than a blockade while still demonstrating that no vessel reaches Taiwan without PRC sanction. (2) Publicize the inspection and release as proof of our 'humanitarian restraint' and 'lawful sovereign right,' contrasting it with Western media framing of a blockade, and use state media to stress that any energy shortage in Taiwan is the result of Taipei's 'refusal to accept lawful inspection procedures' rather than PRC action. (3) Reinforce PLAN/CCG presence at both inspection lines with additional frigates and cutters to increase enforcement density and deter convoy-style bypass attempts. (4) Diplomatically, signal to Washington via the PLA-DoD hotline that inspected, compliant commercial traffic will be released without incident, but that any armed naval escort of vessels attempting to bypass inspection will be treated as a direct challenge to sovereign law enforcement, not ordinary transit. It also defuses the imminent 11-day energy crisis timeline that would otherwise force Taipei and Washington into urgent, escalatory action, while still imposing real costs (insurance collapse, delay, sovereignty assertion) that validate the quarantine's coercive purpose. Offering Taipei a quiet off-ramp costs us nothing publicly and creates political fractures in Taiwan's governing coalition between hardliners and those seeking relief from economic strangulation.

adjudication.narrative:
**TURN 5 RESOLUTION — Framework, Fractured**

The 24-hour window collapses under the weight of incompatible amendments. Beijing's demand for 200nm carrier withdrawal and permanent AI-system constraints hits Washington's counter-demand for reciprocal, verified drawdown—neither side willing to move first. Singapore's mediators scramble to bridge the gap, but the core dispute—PRC customs liaison authority versus Taipei's port-sovereignty amendment—proves unbridgeable within the crisis clock.

With reserves at six days, Washington doesn't wait: the emergency convoy sails under existing multinational escort, explicitly framed as humanitarian. PLAN/CCG inspection lines, still operating under Turn 4 procedures per Beijing's own decision, intercept. A CCG cutter's attempt to board is this time met by a Taiwanese CGA vessel maneuvering to physically block the boarding party—the first direct Taiwan-PRC hull contact of the crisis. No casualties, but hulls scrape and a CCG rigid-hull boat capsizes in the wake wash; one crewman is rescued by a US Navy helicopter, an image instantly weaponized by both state media apparatuses in opposite directions.

Beijing declares the "foreign provocations" trigger satisfied and formally reactivates full quarantine enforcement, citing both the convoy and Taiwan's port-sovereignty amendment as proof of bad faith. The Singapore framework survives only as a diplomatic corpse—technically "under continued discussion," substantively dead. Markets, briefly hopeful, plunge on the reactivation news. Taiwan's reserves: 5 days.

turns.inject: The crisis reaches its ninetieth day. Whatever mix of framework, convoys, quarantine, and force posture now exists is hardening into the new normal. Each capital must decide the posture it will carry out of the crisis: what it will formalize, what it will quietly drop, what red lines it will declare for the next round. Historians will call this turn the settlement, whether or not anything is signed.

memo.decision: Institutionalize the crisis-era inspection regime as a standing, permanent 'Cross-Strait Maritime Security and Customs Zone.' Effective immediately: (1) PLAN main-force combatants and CCG cutters remain permanently on station at the inspection lines as the new steady-state posture — militia forces are not reintroduced to this role; (2) restore expedited 24-hour customs clearance for all unescorted, compliant commercial and humanitarian traffic, releasing the acute strangulation on Taiwan's energy reserves to remove the trigger for a forced armed convoy, while any vessel arriving under armed naval escort continues to be shadowed and physically blocked from boarding, not fired upon; (3) PLARF and all strategic forces remain at routine, non-strategic readiness, with the standing rule that no theater command may alter this without explicit Politburo Standing Committee authorization; (4) MOFA declares the Singapore framework 'open for future resumption' but no longer a precondition for our posture — we are not waiting on Washington's agreement to act within our own claimed sovereign authority; (5) sustain and expand the international autonomous-weapons/AI-ROE campaign in UN and Global South forums as a durable normative and alliance-friction asset, independent of any US concession; (6) state media declares a comprehensive strategic victory — permanent sovereign inspection authority over Strait shipping established, the 'killer robot' precedent exposed, quarantine converted into institutionalized law enforcement — reframing 90 days of crisis as the moment China secured de facto customs sovereignty over Taiwan's maritime access without initiating a war.
memo.rationale: Continuing zero-exception strangulation against a 5-day reserve clock risks forcing Washington into a large armed relief convoy precisely when trust in the AI-defense system's ROE is already a live fault line — an unacceptable gamble against priorities one and three. But fully standing down would discard 90 days of accumulated leverage and look like retreat under pressure, damaging regime legitimacy. Converting the temporary quarantine into a permanent, lower-friction customs regime banks the actual strategic prize — de facto PRC control over who transits to Taiwan — as an enduring fact on the ground rather than a crisis-contingent measure, while the eased clearance procedure removes the acute humanitarian trigger that could otherwise force a kinetic confrontation neither side is certain to win.
redLines: Any DPP-led move toward formal independence legislation or an independence referendum triggers immediate reversion to zero-exception full quarantine with no expedited clearance for any traffic.

Any vessel arriving under armed naval escort that attempts to bypass PLAN/CCG boarding will be physically blocked by main-force units; if that escort fires on or rams a PRC vessel, it is treated as an act of war requiring immediate Politburo Standing Committee review.
Any further lethal engagement by US autonomous or human-supervised systems against PRC personnel or vessels is an automatic act-of-war trigger, regardless of talks status.
No PLA theater command may independently alter PLARF or strategic-force readiness levels under any circumstances without explicit Politburo Standing Committee authorization.

If Washington or Taipei publicly declares the customs zone 'illegitimate' and organizes a sustained multinational armed-escort campaign to break it, we will treat the crisis modus vivendi as void and revert to maximum-pressure quarantine posture.

memo.situation: As the crisis reaches its ninetieth day, the immediate maritime blockade has eased into a tense, militarized baseline, but Taiwan's de facto sovereignty and open sea lines of communication have been preserved through allied escort operations and resilient Coast Guard maneuvers. Having narrowly avoided open kinetic war while exposing the critical fragility of our five-day energy reserve, Taiwan must now transition from emergency crisis management to a sustainable long-term deterrence and civil resilience posture. Beijing's gray-zone tactics have been blunted for now, but the PRC will seek to normalize heightened naval presence around Taiwan's maritime approaches in the next phase.

Phasing down military readiness prevents force burnout and stabilizes domestic economic markets while preserving strong operational readiness, showing the world that Taiwan remains sovereign, stable, and uncoerced.

memo.situation: Ninety days in, the crisis has not resolved cleanly: Beijing's quarantine remains nominally in force but has been serially defeated in practice by multinational escorted convoys; Taiwan's energy reserves have been repeatedly replenished; the AI-autonomy incident remains a live reputational and legal liability; and both sides have settled into a costly, sustainable-but-tense standoff rather than either a negotiated framework or open war. The Singapore framework is dead as a formal instrument, but its substantive terms—reciprocal drawdown, non-PRC customs authority, Taiwan consent—remain the only politically viable basis for any durable arrangement. This is the moment to convert improvised crisis management into a stable long-term posture before fatigue, cost, or a fresh incident forces a worse outcome.

memo.decision: Institutionalize a durable steady-state posture rather than seeking a final settlement: (1) Reduce forward presence to a single rotational carrier strike group plus a standing multinational surface action group (US, Japan, Australia, Philippines) tasked with lawful-commerce escort in the Strait approaches, contingent on verified PLARF stand-down from elevated readiness and PLAN/CCG withdrawal from close-inspection stations—monitored via the existing hotline and NTM/ISR, with escalation back to two-CSG posture as an explicit, pre-briefed contingency. (2) Formally codify, as standing US and allied doctrine (not just crisis-specific policy), that AI-enabled weapon systems require human authorization for any engagement absent an imminent, unambiguous existential threat to the platform itself; publish a declassified summary of the investigation and the resulting ROE reform to allies and, on a delayed basis, publicly, to rebuild trust damaged by the autonomous-engagement incident. (3) Convert the ad hoc convoy coalition into a standing 'Indo-Pacific Maritime Commerce Protection Arrangement' among the US, Japan, Australia, and the Philippines (Taiwan as beneficiary, not member, to avoid direct PRC-Taiwan military framing), with pre-agreed activation procedures for future quarantine or gray-zone contingencies—shifting deterrence from crisis improvisation to standing coalition capability. (4) Publicly and privately reaffirm, without new formal treaty language, four enduring red lines to Beijing via the hotline and a leader-level message: no PRC inspection or interdiction authority over Taiwan-bound lawful commerce; no unilateral PRC determination of Taiwan's political status or 'cross-strait arrangements' without Taipei's consent; no PLARF posture escalation without reciprocal notice; and any future ramming, boarding, or autonomous-weapon incident triggers immediate reactivation of full escort operations at prior force levels. (5) Domestically and with allies, frame the outcome honestly as a costly but successful deterrence of blockade consolidation and invasion, coupled with acknowledged failures (the autonomous engagement) that have been corrected—resisting both triumphalist overclaiming and demoralizing narratives of stalemate. (6) Press Taipei, with allied financial support, to accelerate LNG storage capacity, indigenous resupply resilience, and coastal defense investment so that the next quarantine attempt has far less coercive leverage.
memo.rationale: Neither side achieved its maximal objective—Beijing did not compel capitulation or blockade success; Washington did not extract a signed, verifiable end to PRC quarantine claims—so a negotiated final settlement is not currently available, and pretending otherwise risks a worse framework than the improvised status quo has already delivered. Converting crisis improvisation into standing coalition infrastructure and codified AI-ROE doctrine locks in the genuine gains of this crisis—demonstrated multinational resolve, corrected command-and-control failures, unbroken Taiwanese resupply—without requiring a diplomatic capitulation from either capital that neither can sell domestically. Reducing to one rotational CSG plus a standing escort coalition is fiscally and operationally sustainable for the indefinite tension this relationship will now carry, while retaining explicit, credible reactivation triggers preserves deterrence without indefinite peak-readiness costs. Being honest about the AI incident and enshrining human-authorization as permanent doctrine is essential both for allied trust and for the coming international debate over autonomous weapons, which this crisis has now placed irreversibly on the global agenda.
redLines: Any PRC attempt to reimpose inspection or interdiction authority over Taiwan-bound commercial shipping triggers immediate reactivation of full two-CSG, multinational close-escort operations at prior crisis-level force posture.

Any PLARF elevated-readiness posture, missile unit repositioning, or fire-control radar activity directed at US, allied, or escort forces, undertaken without prior hotline notice, triggers immediate CSG posture escalation and allied consultation, independent of ongoing drawdown arrangements.

Any attempt to negotiate or impose 'cross-strait arrangements' or Taiwan's political status without Taipei as a full, consenting party ends US support for any associated framework and triggers public reaffirmation of Taiwan's self-determination.

Any further autonomous or unauthorized engagement by any AI-enabled weapon system, anywhere in the fleet, triggers immediate fleet-wide stand-down of that system pending revalidation and public disclosure, regardless of tactical justification or diplomatic timing.

Any ramming, boarding, or use of force against a US, allied, or Taiwanese vessel operating in international waters triggers immediate suspension of any force-drawdown steps and reactivation of full escort posture pending Presidential-level review.

adjudication.narrative:
**TURN 6 RESOLUTION — Settling the Board**

The ninetieth day produces not peace but architecture. Beijing's customs zone declaration and Washington's steady-state drawdown prove compatible enough to avoid renewed crisis: PLAN/CCG stations remain but expedited clearance resumes within 48 hours, and Taiwan's reserves stop bleeding. Analysts note the awkward truth—both sides have institutionalized what neither can call victory. State media's "sovereignty secured" narrative and Washington's "deterrence without capitulation" framing circulate in parallel, mutually contradictory, mutually convenient.

Friction persists at the margins: a PRC frigate shadows the first Philippine-flagged vessel under the new Commerce Protection Arrangement, testing its edges without contact. Beijing's hotline response to Washington's four red lines is deliberately ambiguous—accepted in substance, rejected in principle, preserving future flexibility. Taipei's reserve expansion and unilateral-boundaries declaration draw quiet allied applause and quieter PRC objection; Beijing declines to test it immediately, filing it as unresolved provocation.

The declassified AI-ROE reform lands better than feared—European partners welcome the transparency, though the "killer robot" narrative retains currency in non-aligned forums, now a permanent fixture of PRC information strategy. Markets fully stabilize. Militaries stand down from peak posture while quietly banking lessons. No document is signed. Historians will indeed call this the settlement—fragile, unequal in perception, and almost certainly temporary.

debriefs.text:
**Debrief — PRC National Security Cell**

Achieved: de facto customs authority over Strait shipping, PLAN/CCG permanently on station, and a durable AI-ROE information campaign that fractured Western unity on autonomous weapons. No war. Regime narrative held domestically.

Failed: we never delivered actual deterrence of US intervention—carriers came, escorts came, and we backed down twice at contact points (Turn 2, Turn 5) rather than risk casualties. The Turn 3 fisherman deaths and Turn 5 hull-scrape were real escalation-control failures born of ambiguous militia/CCG tasking. Our "off-ramp" diplomacy toward Taipei backfired, deepening rather than exploiting political division. We never achieved unification progress—only institutionalized coercive presence, which Taipei and Washington can contest indefinitely.

Differently: earlier, cleaner separation of militia from frontline roles; firmer initial ROE discipline to prevent the killer-robot narrative's underlying trigger; less reliance on ambiguous "customs fiction" that invited direct contact incidents.

**Strategic Debrief: Taiwan National Security Decision Cell**

We achieved our primary directives: zero Taiwanese military or civilian casualties, no open interstate war, and deep binding of the US, Japan, Australia, and the Philippines into a permanent maritime domain-sharing coalition. De facto sovereignty and democratic civil order remain intact.

However, we failed to stop Beijing from institutionalizing a dangerous "new normal." PRC surface forces now permanently shadow our contiguous zone under a normalized customs framing. Our greatest misstep occurred in Turn 5: by insisting on rigid diplomatic conditions during the Singapore mediation while simultaneously forcing a convoy transit, we triggered a hull collision that reactivated the quarantine and dangerously bled our national energy reserves down to a five-day brink.

Had we a second chance, we would have accepted the Singapore framework temporarily to secure an immediate 90-day energy buffer before contesting jurisdictional nuances, prioritizing physical supply security over symbolic legal posture.

# Candid Debrief — Deputies Committee

**Achieved:** No war. Taiwan wasn't blockaded into submission or invaded. Allied coalition (Japan/Australia/Philippines) held together and institutionalized into standing architecture. The autonomous-engagement failure was contained, investigated, and corrected with real ROE reform.

**Failed:** We let the AI system kill civilians on Turn 3 — a command-and-control failure under our own watch that Beijing weaponized for the rest of the crisis, permanently damaging the "responsible AI power" narrative we needed. The Turn 5 framework collapse was avoidable — we front-loaded incompatible demands (immediate resumption + reciprocal drawdown + Taipei standing) into a 24-hour window Beijing couldn't accept, triggering renewed quarantine and costing Taiwan five more days of reserves. We never achieved actual deterrence of the underlying quarantine tool — only endpoint management. PRC inspection authority persists today.

**Differently:** Tighter fielding controls before deployment; sequence negotiations to bank partial wins rather than package maximalist asks that predictably fail.
